text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call (priority: P1). Rapid increase in 5xxs for prefix/KV cache path on prod-usw2. Affected model: rdx-text-v2, tenant slice: acme-inc. Error rate + latency spike started ~2m ago. Logs show repeated KV cache misses and fallback thrash.
Maya Chen: on it, grabbing runbook. First reaction: do we need to throttle incoming traffic or flip cache bypass for correctness?
Sam Ortiz: seeing same in tracing. KV store latency to redis-cluster-3 is spiking 4-6x; cache miss rate went from 2%->28%. Likely hot prefix eviction due to rolling quantization job yesterday.
Priya Nair: tagging infra now. If KV is degraded, we should avoid cascading retries. Recommend temporary rate-limit per-tenant and disable prefetch/backfill to reduce pressure.
Alex Gomez: customers on the thread: acme-support pinged about 50% failed chat requests. Need clear ETA for mitigation and customer-facing message.
Maya Chen: plan: 1) apply tenant-level throttles for acme-inc (reduce concurrency), 2) disable prefix prefetch and prefix-cache write-through for rdx-text-v2 on prod-usw2, 3) enable cache-bypass header for correctness for requests that opt-in, 4) monitor for error drop.
Sam Ortiz: will apply throttle and flip prefetch. Executing now:
```bash
# reduce concurrency & token rate for tenant
redwoodctl traffic limit set --tenant acme-inc --region prod-usw2 --concurrency 12 --rps 40
# disable prefix prefetch for model variant
redwoodctl model config patch rdx-text-v2 --region prod-usw2 --set prefix_prefetch=false
```
Sam Ortiz: throttle applied. Pre-fetch disabled. Observability: 5xx rate down ~45% in last 30s, p95 latency improving but still elevated.
Priya Nair: also deploying KV fallback mode: switch writes to async and reduce TTL for hot keys to avoid thrash. Applying small change to cache write strategy.
```json
{"cache_write_mode":"async","hot_ttl_seconds":30}
```
Maya Chen: disabled write-through for prefix cache and set bypass header available for correctness. Note: disabling write-through may cause slight cold-start regressions but avoids overloaded KV.
Sam Ortiz: added temporary traffic-shaping policy to route ~30% of new requests to rdx-text-v2-fallback (quantized variant with local in-memory cache) to reduce KV pressure.
deploy-bot: Deployment rdx-text-v2-fallback v2025.11 canary started (10% route). :rocket:
Alex Gomez: telling acme-support we have a mitigation in place; errors reduced, SLA impact limited to degraded latency for a subset. Sending update now.
Maya Chen: quick handoff — Priya, I'll need you on follow-up for the KV cluster. I'm going offline in 15m, Sam will be primary on runtime changes.
Priya Nair: ack — I'll open a follow-up incident to track KV repro and postmortem. First priority is to restore normal KV latency and then re-enable prefix prefetch gradually.
Sam Ortiz: monitoring dashboards show steady improvement; 5xxs down to baseline ~5% over pre-incident. Removing tenant throttle will be a phased rollback.
Maya Chen: rollback checklist: 1) undo tenant concurrency limiter, 2) re-enable prefix_prefetch=false->true in small incremental steps, 3) re-evaluate hot key eviction policy and quantization job timing.
Sam Ortiz: rolling back throttle for acme-inc to 70% of original at t+10m for safety. Command:
```bash
redwoodctl traffic limit set --tenant acme-inc --region prod-usw2 --concurrency 40 --rps 120
```
Sam Ortiz: throttle eased. 5xxs stable.
Maya Chen: official incident summary for customers and postmortem will be drafted by Priya and me. Immediate mitigations: tenant throttle, disabled prefetch & write-through, cache-bypass option, traffic-shift to fallback quantized model. Root cause hypothesis: KV latency spike from background quantization backfill causing hot key eviction and elevated miss storms.
Alex Gomez: sending note to acme-support: "Mitigations applied; we observed error rate drop and are monitoring. We'll follow up with a postmortem and ETA for full recovery." :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident resolved (P1 -> monitoring). Close if no further regressions in 30m.
Maya Chen: closing here, moving to postmortem doc. Thanks all for quick responses. :pray:
